title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 293–650, 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'): Grothendieck builds a group scheme M_{ρ,σ} over a base S. It is an algebraic 'envelope' of the modular group, generated by a reductive group G (with SG ≃ 𝔊^+_{ρ,σ}, an Sl_2-type group) together with tori T_ρ (attached to the order-3/6 element ρ) and the normaliser N'_σ of a torus (attached to σ, dihedral D_4 on Z-points). On the previous page he records M_{ρ,σ}(Z) ≃ (Z/6 × D_4)·Sl(2,Z), a semidirect product.

On this page:
(57) He defines a homomorphism Θ: M_{ρ,σ} → G. On the subgroup 𝔊^+_{ρ,σ} ≃ SG it is the identity. On the 'stabiliser' subgroup M_{ρ,σ}(0) ⊂ T_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ it is the projection (u,a,b) ↦ u. Here M(0) is a subgroup of the product cut out by determinant compatibilities.
(58) The same formula holds on the larger subgroup M[0] ⊂ B'_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ, with B'_0 a Borel-type group containing T_0.
(59) Every element of G-component 1 lies in M(0) (cartesian square), so Ker Θ = {(1,a,b) : det b = 1, (det a)^2 = 1}. This is S'T_ρ × SN'_σ, where SN'_σ = Ker(det: N'_σ → G_m) and S'T_ρ = {a : (det a)^2 = 1}.
(60)–(61) Restrict to the neutral component: Θ° = Θ|M°. This gives an exact sequence 1 → Ker Θ° → Ker Θ → μ_2 × μ_2 → 1. The map to μ_2 × μ_2 is (sign of det a, component of b in π_0(N'_σ)). Hence Ker Θ° ≃ ST_ρ × ST_σ, the norm-one subtori. A crossed-out attempt identifies this with Rad(M°) ≃ Centre°(M°).
(62) He sets SR°_{ρ,σ} = 1 × ST_ρ × ST_σ = Ker Θ° = Ker Θ ∩ M°. It is central in M°. The next page adds that it is normal but not central in M.

Purpose (completed on the next page): M/SR° ≃ G × μ_2 × μ_2, via (Θ, ε_1, ε_2). So M_{ρ,σ} is an extension of G × μ_2 × μ_2 by a two-dimensional torus. This is a structure theorem for his group-scheme model of the genus-1 / modular stage of the Teichmüller tower and the relations ρ^3 = σ^2 = 1.
errors: No real mathematical error is visible. The quotient Ker Θ/Ker Θ° is written μ_2 × μ_2, but the σ-factor is naturally π_0(N'_σ) ≃ Z/2 (constant). Z/2 and μ_2 agree only when 2 is invertible on S, a caveat he himself flags on the previous page for characteristic 2.
The identification of Ker Θ° with Rad(M°) ≃ Centre°(M°) was crossed out, apparently because it was not justified.

ideas.what: A group scheme M_{ρ,σ} over Spec Z whose Z-points are (Z/6 × D_4) ⋉ Sl(2,Z), with an explicit retraction Θ onto G and the kernel computed
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic group-scheme envelope (an extension of a reductive group by tori and finite groups) of the modular group with torsion
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard attribution; related to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps) but not the same object
ideas.where_published: Only the motivating 'équation des lacets' is hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche (unsure about the details)

ideas.what: Kernel computation Ker Θ ≃ S'T_ρ × SN'_σ and the exact sequence with μ_2 × μ_2 via determinant and component maps
ideas.modern_name: Component group and neutral component of a kernel; norm-one subtori

ideas.what: The central torus SR° ⊂ M° and the splitting M/SR° ≃ G × μ_2 × μ_2
ideas.modern_name: Structure of a non-connected group scheme as a torus extension of G × (finite)

missed.claim: The page belongs to a sustained unpublished construction of an algebraic group scheme over Z modelling the modular group with its torsion elements ρ, σ, as a step toward the 'loop equation' relations. That construction does not seem to have been taken up in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller literature, which works with profinite or pro-unipotent completions instead.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An algebraic group scheme over Z encoding the (Z/6 × D_4) ⋉ Sl(2,Z) structure could give an arithmetic, non-completed framework for the order-3 and order-2 relations in GT-type groups. The page itself is a routine computation within that framework.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine kernel and extension computation. Its interest lies only in being part of the largely unknown programme of algebraic envelopes of the modular group in the 'équation des lacets' notes.
transcription_corrections: In (57) and (59), 'M_{ρ,σ}(0) ≃ T_0×T_ρ×N'_σ' should read '⊂' (it is a subgroup, which is why the kernel has determinant constraints).
The margin reads something like 'θ_i^θ ... θ_i, θ' with a circled '40' (folio number), not meaningful formulas.
In (61) the map label may be (ε_1, ε_2) as on the next page rather than (ε_3, ε_2); the image is ambiguous.
The crossed-out line reads '(Rad(M°_{ρ,σ}) ≃ Centre°(M°_{ρ,σ}))', and the struck word above it is 'Centre'.
In (62), 'qui est un sous-groupe central de M°_{ρ,σ} (il est' continues on the next page as 'distingué mais pas central dans M_{ρ,σ}'.
